jobs.title: Director, Finance & Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE:
Director, Finance and Business Intelligence
STATUS:
Permanent, Full Time
LOCATION:
Home Office Based
Candidates are required to reside in the province of Ontario or National Capital Region, maintain a private and safe workspace, and have a high-quality internet connection.
HOURS OF WORK:
35 hours/week (regular office hours)
GRADE:
Grade 11
The hiring range for this position ranges from $166,261.26 to $182,887.39, with the opportunity to grow within the broader salary range as you advance in your role.

About Us

Workplace Safety & Prevention Services (WSPS) is a not-for-profit organization committed to protecting Ontario’s workers and businesses. It serves more than 174,000 member firms and 4.2 million workers across the agricultural, manufacturing and service sectors. A proud partner in the province’s occupational health and safety system and a trusted safety advisor since 1917, WSPS has a rich history of making workplaces safer.

Our focus on healthy workplaces extends to our own strong safety culture. We’re committed to helping employees thrive in a remote-first world, and we’re honoured to be recognized as a Great Place to Work for two consecutive years for 2024 and 2025.

Why Work with WSPS

As a member of our team, you'll benefit from a compensation package aimed at keeping you happy, healthy, motivated and safe. Highlights include:
Make a meaningful impact by supporting our mission to protect Ontario’s workers and businesses
35-hour work week
Flexible working arrangements within the province of Ontario
Comprehensive life and health benefits (100% company paid Health & Dental)
Defined Benefit Pension Plan
Generous vacation and leave entitlements (including paid time off over Christmas and New Year's, paid parental leave benefits)
Internet allowance
And more!

Role

Reporting to the CFO and Vice President, Corporate Services, this position is responsible for the strategic planning, leadership and oversight of the Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence functions. The Director, Finance and Business Intelligence will work as a member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to support the achievement of the WSPS strategic plan. As future focused leader, this role plays an integral part in formulating best practices and process improvements while leveraging technology and tools for financial planning, accounting services, financial and business reporting.

Responsibilities

Note: Percentages refer to approximate % of time spent on each area, over the course of a given year.
1. TEAM LEADERSHIP, DEVELOPMENT AND ADMINISTRATION (20%)

Provide leadership to Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence managers. Guide and coach team members to effectively perform and achieve objectives.
Ensure the development of a highly skilled, knowledgeable, and motivated workforce in the team.
Ensure team structures, positions and skills are appropriate for delivery of the team’s and organization’s mandate.
Provide the necessary training, resources, and support to ensure that team members are continually developing and enhancing their capabilities.
Evaluate and lead the team through succession planning to ensure continuity in roles.
Review and analyze engagement results with a focus on solutions to increase employee engagement in satisfaction in the department. Assure strong employee engagement/satisfaction results in the department.
Collaborate with the team to ensure clear understanding and alignment related to changes within the organization.
Reinforces the WSPS vision and employees’ connection to that vision.
Lead multi-disciplinary project teams as needed.
Upholds and promotes ethical standards, integrity, and a strong sense of corporate responsibility as per WSPS policies and procedures.

2. RELATIONSHIP BUILDING (20%)

Develop strong customer and stakeholder relationships with all divisions/business units in the organization to support financial management, business intelligence processes, and continuous improvement efforts at WSPS.
Act as a liaison between WSPS and the Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD), representing WSPS’ interests while developing collaborative and effective relationships.

3. LEADERSHIP OF ACCOUNTING SERVICE DELIVERY (20%)

Lead the team responsible for the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of internal controls to safeguard the assets of WSPS and to mitigate business risks.
Review existing/new/proposed accounting policies to assess adherence to GAAP and well as consider operational impacts.
Oversee the preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual internal and Board of Director financial statements, as well as preparation of annual external financial statements, ensuring the format and disclosure within statements are effective for decision-making, while adhering to GAAP requirements.
Identify areas for improvement in current systems required to comply with TPA reporting requirements and partner with appropriate functional areas to implement improvements.
Participate in TPA audit relating to both financial information provided to the Ministry and reporting of performance indicators.
Ensure effectiveness and efficiency of internal monitoring processes that assess accounting transactions for validity, completeness, accuracy and adherence to all government directives and WSPS policies to minimize risk of loss.
Ensure procurement policies and procedures comply with government directives.
Ensure consistent training and advice on procurement activities are communicated across the organization, including monitoring of emerging requirements as mandated by government for implementation and compliance.
Act as liaison with government agencies on procurement reporting requirements.
Participate in the design and management of an investment strategy to achieve strategic and financial goals of WSPS, including meeting cash flow requirements, while adhering to parameters set by government directives and internal policies.

4. LEADERSHIP OF BUDGETING, FINANCIAL REPORTING AND AUDIT PROCESS (20%)

Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely annual budget process and provide leadership to the organization in the preparation of an annual budget that adheres to ministry requirements.
Serve as liaison between WSPS and the Ministry for financial planning and Transfer Payment Agreement (TPA) reporting related matters.
Provide guidance to the executive and senior leadership teams during the budgeting process to achieve a balanced budget.
Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely forecasting process, including reporting to senior management in support of effective decision-making.
Oversee the preparation of forecast and spending reports, ensuring they are effective in communicating the organization’s financial position, highlighting any areas of risk, and recommending mitigation strategies.
Provide advice and develop recommendations on financial management practices across the organization.
Oversee monthly and quarterly variance analysis and develop recommendations for achieving a balanced budget at year-end.
Oversee analysis and develop recommendations on sales, contribution margins and pricing strategies.
Lead development of Ministry reporting packages, including annual business plan and quarterly reports, ensuring they meet all requirements.
Work closely with the external actuary in the annual employee future benefits valuation process to ensure accurate data is reflected in the valuation results and the reports are available for year-end audit and budgeting purposes.
Oversee the team leading the audit preparation process to ensure audit process and procedures performed are effective and efficient and to identify areas where documents/procedures can be updated to facilitate a more efficient audit process.
At year end audit, ensure appropriate documentation/supporting documents are available for auditor’s review and act as liaison between auditor and other WSPS departments where ownership of supporting information/documents does not lie within Corporate Services.
Stay current on financial standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations to ensure financial record systems are maintained in accordance with the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), as well as the designated standards of the government bodies.

5. LEADERSHIP OF BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE (20%)

Oversee the collection, synthesis and analysis of data and metrics to inform senior management decision making, priority setting and investment strategies.
Regularly assess processes and systems used for the collection, synthesis, and analysis of data to promote effectiveness and efficiency.
Oversee the preparation of ministry reports ensuring all requirements are met, highlighting areas of potential under performance, and developing recommendations to address.
Oversee development of reporting tools, including dashboards and scorecards, that provide useful and timely information for decision making, as well as measure and report on the impact and value of WSPS activities.
Report on key performance metrics that show progress WSPS’ strategy and mandate and communicate the results across WSPS.
Oversee development and application of a WSPS framework for acquiring business intelligence on the market, industry, and our customers, to inform decision-making and business planning. Framework includes quantitative measurements, customer feedback and environmental scans.
Develop and promote tools and best practices for project management with a view to develop competencies across the organization.
Oversee project management professionals to ensure effective support of enterprise-wide or high priority projects to ensure effective, timely and efficient implementation.

5. CONTRIBUTES TO A HEALTHY AND SAFE WORK ENVIRONMENT (at all times)

Adhere to WSPS policies, procedures, process fact sheets, guidelines, and business rules.
Contribute to the promotion of a healthy & safe culture through modelling and following WSPS health, safety and wellness policies and practices.
Act as a role model internally and externally by demonstrating knowledge of health and safety and wellness practices, weighing options for sound risk management decision making.

Skills & Experience

Minimum

Bachelor’s degree in business or related field, or minimum of 5 years of related experience in financial management.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) Designation
5-7 years progressive management experience with emphasis on financial planning and reporting, exposure to senior management decision making, developing talent, and managing budgets.
Experience leading across multiple teams to deliver service excellence.
Excellent collaboration skills to effectively engage with internal and external stakeholders.
Excellent oral and written communication, including ability to present complex concepts in simple business-oriented terms.

Preferred

10+ years progressive management experience in a not-for-profit environment
Experience leading positive change and seeking out continuous improvement.
Understanding Transfer Payment Agreement model and requirements
This position requires frequent travel within the Mississauga area and thus it is preferred that candidates live within 75km of WSPS’ Mississauga Head Office.

Additional Requirements

Candidates are required to reside in the province of Ontario (or National Capital Region), maintain a private and safe workspace, and have a high-quality internet connection.
Provide an original criminal background check at your own expense prior to commencing work with WSPS. The criminal record check document must have been issued no more than 30 days prior to first day of employment.
To support success in building connections, inclusion and collaboration, a minimum level of in person presence for the purposes of meetings is required for all team members as of July 2026:
Divisional Meetings on a quarterly basis.
Team Meetings on a month

jobs.company: CENGN - (Centre of Excellence in Next Generation Networks)
jobs.title: Head, Strategy and Business Development
jobs.description:
Position:
Head, Strategy and Business Development
Location:
Ottawa 
Reports to:
President & CEO
Salary range:
$165,000 - $185,000
Vacancy Status:
This posting is for a new vacancy. We are hiring for 1 position.

Job Summary / Overview: 

The Head, Strategy and Business Development plays a central role in shaping CENGN’s strategic direction and driving its evolution, accelerating commercialization and technology adoption for Canada’s innovation economy. This position combines strategic foresight with business development leadership, linking market intelligence, partnership development, and execution to deliver tangible , measurable results for CENGN and the ecosystem we serve.

As a key advisor to the President & CEO, this role will lead the design and delivery of CENGN’s strategic roadmap, ensuring alignment with emerging technologies and national priorities across 5G, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, and defence innovation. You will identify and develop new revenue opportunities, forge strategic alliances, and position CENGN as a trusted partner to industry, government, academia, and defence organizations.

This role also focuses on building and leading a high-performing business development team, strengthening member engagement, and enabling cross-functional collaboration so strategy, execution, and partnership development work together to enhance CENGN’s reputation across the ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities:  

Strategy
Lead the annual and multi-year strategic planning cycle in close partnership with the CEO, ensuring priorities are grounded in market reality, financial sustainability, and CENGN's mission
Track competitive, regulatory, and technology shifts, particularly in 5G, cloud, AI, and digital infrastructure and translate these into actionable strategic recommendations
Identify and evaluate new revenue streams, partnership models, and market opportunities that advance CENGN's path to long-term sustainability
Develop operational frameworks for evaluating strategic partnerships, alliances, and new service areas
Deepen relationships with funding partners and ensure organizational accountability for outcomes under government or partner funding agreements.
Provide the CEO and executive team with clear, evidence-based strategic counsel on major decisions

Business Development
Lead, mentor, and grow the Business Development team, setting clear direction while empowering individual ownership
Through leadership of the team, maintain and deepen existing member and partner relationships
Identify and pursue sustainable revenue opportunities, including 3rd party testing, training, and commercial services
Foster alliances with like-minded organizations locally, nationally, and internationally
Lead and manage business development pipeline activity with discipline; tracking leads, advancing opportunities, and keeping leadership informed
Stay current on industry trends and engage CENGN's broader ecosystem through events, social channels, and sector initiatives

Cross-Functional Leadership
Champion a culture of transparency with no silos and no surprises.
Demonstrate and support our CENGN values of integrity, accountability, agility, collaboration and fostering success 
Bring solutions and decisions to the table with context, connected to our mission

What We're Looking For

Experience
10–15 years of progressive experience in the Information and Communications Technology or digital infrastructure sector
Demonstrated track record in business development. You know how to open doors and close deals
Experience leading or significantly contributing to strategic planning in a technology-driven organization
Proven ability to build, lead and work cross-functionally to support high-performing teams 
Bilingualism (English/French) is a strong asset

Competencies
Commercial acumen paired with genuine strategic thinking, you understand both the numbers and the narrative
Strong communicator and relationship builder across diverse stakeholder groups including government, industry, academia, and start-ups
Comfortable operating with ambiguity and in a fast-moving environment with shifting priorities
High emotional intelligence.  You can read rooms, build trust, and bring people along
Proficiency in CRM tools, MS Office, and presentation platforms

Education
Bachelor's degree with either a Business or Technology focus, or equivalent experience; MBA or advanced degree an asset

This role does not include leadership of the Marketing function. It is also not a role where success is measured by activity alone. The expectation is strategic clarity, high performance teams and team cohesion, and revenue results. Anyone coming in will be expected to invest time in understanding CENGN's existing culture, relationships, and ways of working before reshaping any of them.

Successful applicants must meet all applicable security requirements, including but not limited to the ability to obtain and maintain a Canadian government security clearance. Applicants may be required to meet additional security requirements in order to gain access to technical data, classified areas or information. You must be eligible to work in Canada.

Interested and qualified candidates are invited to forward their resume in confidence to CENGN via CENGN’s Application Portal. CENGN thanks all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be acknowledged. CENGN is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Associate Director S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics
jobs.description:
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.

Job Purpose

This role exists to strengthen how the North America Foods business plans, decides, and delivers across demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and business waste. As Associate Director, S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics, you will lead the planning excellence and analytics agenda that connects business ambition with practical, reliable operating plans. You will help build a more resilient, data-driven, and collaborative supply chain that enables trusted Foods brands to serve customers and consumers with confidence. This is inclusive of planning technology, analytics, and process.

You will be part of a team that believes planning is more than a process. It is a critical way of bringing people together, making better decisions, and creating the conditions for sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead the development and continuous improvement of integrated planning and sales and operations planning practices across North America Foods (Retail and Foods Solutions; US and Canada). You will partner closely with Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Material Planning, Manufacturing, Finance, Customer Development, Marketing, and senior Supply Chain leaders to ensure the business has clear plans, strong governance, reporting/tools, and actionable insights to support growth, service, efficiency, and transformation.

Lead a team of WL1s/2s to drive the sales and operations planning excellence agenda. Ensure robust process and technology are in place to ensure demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and financial assumptions are connected through clear business rhythms and decision-making forums.
Partner with integrated planning teams to identify risks, opportunities, and gaps within planning technology/process and drive improvement plans. Identify / build business cases or drive cross functional process improvement.
Strengthen integrated planning capability by improving processes, tools, routines, governance, and ways of working across the North America Foods planning community.
Lead planning performance management, including the maintenance and creation and use of clear measures, scorecards, dashboards, reports, and insights that help teams make faster and better decisions. This can include modifying existing dashboards due to new business insights
Drive continuous improvement, simplification, and standardization across planning processes to improve reliability, reduce complexity, and support scalable ways of working.
Act as the primary point of contact for Planning TSAs.
Support the transition to the future Foods organization by helping design, build, and embed planning capabilities that enable business continuity from day one and maturity over time.
Build trusted relationships across functions and levels, creating a collaborative planning culture where teams are aligned, accountable, and focused on shared outcomes.

What The First Year Looks Like

During the first year, you will play a visible role in building planning excellence for the future North America Foods organization. You will learn the current planning landscape, connect with key partners across the business, and help establish the routines, measures, and decision-making forums needed to support business continuity and performance.

In your first few months, you will focus on understanding the end-to-end planning processes, key business priorities, current pain points, and transition requirements. You will build relationships with the planning community, data/tech teams, and cross-functional partners, assess existing tools and processes, and identify where stronger governance or simplification is needed.

As the year progresses, you will lead improvements to planning routines, performance reporting, and sales and operations planning governance. You will help teams align on clear roles, timelines, inputs, decisions, and escalation paths, while supporting capability-building across the planning organization.

By the end of the first year, you will have helped create a stronger integrated planning foundation for North America Foods, with clearer decision-making, improved planning visibility, stronger cross-functional alignment, and practical tools that support service, inventory, cost, waste reduction, and growth.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Engineering, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Significant experience 10y+ in integrated planning, demand planning, supply planning, business planning, supply chain transformation, or related end-to-end supply chain roles.
Strong understanding of sales and operations planning, forecasting, inventory management, capacity planning, supply planning, service management, and business waste reduction.
Experience leading cross-functional planning decisions and balancing service, inventory, cost, responsiveness, and growth priorities.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear business recommendations.
Experience influencing senior stakeholders and leading change in a complex, fast-moving environment.
Demonstrated ability to build capability, improve processes, and create practical ways of working that teams can adopt and sustain.
Strong understanding of planning tools and technology including back end master data.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in consumer goods, food and beverage, manufacturing, retail, or another complex supply chain environment.
Experience leading sales and operations planning improvements, integrated planning transformation, or planning excellence programs across multiple teams or markets.
Experience with advanced planning systems, enterprise resource planning systems, business intelligence tools, or planning analytics platforms.
Experience supporting organization transition, business separation, integration, or large-scale transformation activities.
Advanced degree or professional certification in supply chain, operations, planning, project management, or continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) & Co-founder - AI for Small Law Firms
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

AI is changing the economics of legal practice. Work that once took hours can increasingly be done in minutes, creating both enormous leverage for lawyers and new pressure to win and serve more clients efficiently.

Yet solo practitioners and small law firms still operate with many of the same constraints: missed calls, slow follow-up, intake handled between client matters, inconsistent marketing, and administrative work competing with billable time. Building larger intake, administrative, and marketing teams is expensive and increasingly unnecessary.

BloomLex is building a different model: a managed AI workforce that helps small law firms grow without growing their team.

The customer thesis has been validated through live pilots, and multiple deployments are moving into production evaluation. The next phase is proving in-production reliability, delivery economics, repeatability, and scalability. The companies that successfully deploy trusted AI workers into professional-service verticals over the next 18 months have an opportunity to define entirely new categories. We intend to be one of them.

The Venture

BloomLex is building an AI workforce for solo practitioners and small law firms, helping them win and serve more clients without adding headcount.

We call the broader shift the Rise of the Solo: AI gives an individual lawyer or small firm access to capabilities that historically required a much larger organization.

Unlike self-serve software, BloomLex is fully managed. We configure, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve the AI workforce for each firm. Our customers evaluate us on outcomes — calls answered, prospective clients captured, consultations booked, demand generated, follow-up completed, and time saved — not on how much software they configure themselves.

Our AI workforce starts with two teammates:

Ava — AI Front Desk. Ava answers calls 24/7, handles structured intake, screens and routes inquiries, books consultations, performs outbound callbacks and follow-up, and integrates those interactions into the firm's workflow.

Claire — AI Marketing Assistant. Claire helps firms generate and nurture demand through content, digital marketing, campaign management and optimization, lead nurturing, and ongoing marketing execution.

Together, Ava and Claire address both sides of growth: Claire helps create demand; Ava helps ensure that demand is captured and converted.

They are also the beginning, not the end, of the platform. Our roadmap expands the AI workforce across the operational side of the practice — including custom workflows and additional specialized AI roles — all delivered through the same managed model and coordinated around the lawyer.

The Partnership

The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, live pilots are running, and the technology and deployment infrastructure are being built for scale.

What remains is to complete the founding team with a commercial co-founder — someone who will own revenue and go-to-market with the same conviction, urgency, and sense of ownership as the CEO and CTO.

This is not a role where you inherit a sales team, a mature playbook, and a predictable funnel. You will help discover and build those things.

You will personally close early customers, determine which channels scale, refine the commercial model from real market evidence, and then build the organization capable of repeating it.

This is a co-founder and leadership role, not simply a sales hire. You will join the CEO and CTO as one of three co-founders, with founder-level equity, founder-level responsibility, and a meaningful voice in go-to-market, pricing, hiring, fundraising, product direction, and company strategy.

What You'll Own

As Co-Founder & CRO, you will own the commercial journey from first conversation through acquisition, retention, and expansion.

Early Revenue — Personally convert pilots and prospects into paying customers and establish the first repeatable sales motion across solo practitioners and firms of up to five lawyers.
Go-to-Market — Refine and operationalize our ICP, positioning, messaging, and Rise of the Solo narrative, turning them into outreach, demos, pipeline, and closed revenue.
Pipeline & Channels — Determine which acquisition channels actually work — outbound, content, paid acquisition, referrals, partnerships, communities, events, and others — and concentrate resources behind the ones that can scale.
Partnerships & Distribution — Build relationships with legal business coaches, bar associations, legal communities, consultants, complementary technology providers, and other potential distribution partners.
Pricing & Commercial Economics — Own pricing, packaging, expansion strategy, customer acquisition economics, retention targets, and the path toward increasing revenue per firm as the AI workforce expands.
Customer Success & Retention — Stay close to early customers, understand why they buy and why they stay, and build the commercial processes that turn adoption into retention, expansion, referrals, and advocacy.
Customer Proof — Turn early wins into measurable case studies, testimonials, references, and commercial proof around the outcomes lawyers care about.
Fundraising — Help tell the growth story to investors through credible traction, metrics, unit economics, forecasts, and a clear path to scale.
Team — Once the motion is working, recruit and lead the sales, partnerships, and customer-success organization needed to scale it.

Co-Founder Profile

We're looking for a builder first and a sales executive second.

You are likely someone who has spent enough time inside an established company to know how a professional revenue organization works — but would rather build one than inherit one.

You should bring:

A strong record of full-cycle selling, ideally into the legal market or another fragmented SMB/professional-services vertical.
The confidence to personally prospect, run demos, negotiate, close, onboard, and expand early customers before hiring people to do it for you.
A strong understanding of how small-business buyers make decisions, what creates trust, and how to turn an early-stage product into a compelling commercial proposition.
Ideally, an existing network within legal technology, solo and small-firm legal communities, bar associations, legal services, or adjacent channels.
Strong commercial judgment — including the willingness to challenge assumptions about positioning, pricing, channels, or markets when the evidence says we should.
Entrepreneurial drive: you are ready to move from selling someone else's company to building one of your own.
Comfort with an early-stage compensation model weighted heavily toward ownership and revenue creation rather than a conventional executive salary.
The ability to operate as a principal, not an employee — making decisions with the long-term value of the company in mind and doing whatever work is necessary at this stage to move it forward.

Early-stage go-to-market leadership, experience selling AI or automation products, and experience selling into the legal profession are strongly preferred. Candidates should be able to operate effectively across North American time zones.

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

Together, Ava and Claire address both sides of growth: Claire helps create demand; Ava helps ensure that demand is captured and converted.

They are also the beginning, not the end, of the platform. Our roadmap expands the AI workforce across the operational side of the practice — including custom workflows and additional specialized AI roles — all delivered through the same managed model and coordinated around the lawyer.

The Partnership

The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, live pilots are running, and the technology and deployment infrastructure are being built for scale.

What remains is to complete the founding team with a commercial co-founder — someone who will own revenue and go-to-market with the same conviction, urgency, and sense of ownership as the CEO and CTO.

This is not a role where you inherit a sales team, a mature playbook, and a predictable funnel. You will help discover and build those things.

You will personally close early customers, determine which channels scale, refine the commercial model from real market evidence, and then build the organization capable of repeating it.

This is a co-founder and leadership role, not simply a sales hire. You will join the CEO and CTO as one of three co-founders, with founder-level equity, founder-level responsibility, and a meaningful voice in go-to-market, pricing, hiring, fundraising, product direction, and company strategy.

What You'll Own

As Co-Founder & CRO, you will own the commercial journey from first conversation through acquisition, retention, and expansion.

Early Revenue — Personally convert pilots and prospects into paying customers and establish the first repeatable sales motion across solo practitioners and firms of up to five lawyers.
Go-to-Market — Refine and operationalize our ICP, positioning, messaging, and Rise of the Solo narrative, turning them into outreach, demos, pipeline, and closed revenue.
Pipeline & Channels — Determine which acquisition channels actually work — outbound, content, paid acquisition, referrals, partnerships, communities, events, and others — and concentrate resources behind the ones that can scale.
Partnerships & Distribution — Build relationships with legal business coaches, bar associations, legal communities, consultants, complementary technology providers, and other potential distribution partners.
Pricing & Commercial Economics — Own pricing, packaging, expansion strategy, customer acquisition economics, retention targets, and the path toward increasing revenue per firm as the AI workforce expands.
Customer Success & Retention — Stay close to early customers, understand why they buy and why they stay, and build the commercial processes that turn adoption into retention, expansion, referrals, and advocacy.
Customer Proof — Turn early wins into measurable case studies, testimonials, references, and commercial proof around the outcomes lawyers care about.
Fundraising — Help tell the growth story to investors through credible traction, metrics, unit economics, forecasts, and a clear path to scale.
Team — Once the motion is working, recruit and lead the sales, partnerships, and customer-success organization needed to scale it.

Co-Founder Profile

We're looking for a builder first and a sales executive second.

You are likely someone who has spent enough time inside an established company to know how a professional revenue organization works — but would rather build one than inherit one.

You should bring:

A strong record of full-cycle selling, ideally into the legal market or another fragmented SMB/professional-services vertical.
The confidence to personally prospect, run demos, negotiate, close, onboard, and expand early customers before hiring people to do it for you.
A strong understanding of how small-business buyers make decisions, what creates trust, and how to turn an early-stage product into a compelling commercial proposition.
Ideally, an existing network within legal technology, solo and small-firm legal communities, bar associations, legal services, or adjacent channels.
Strong commercial judgment — including the willingness to challenge assumptions about positioning, pricing, channels, or markets when the evidence says we should.
Entrepreneurial drive: you are ready to move from selling someone else's company to building one of your own.
Comfort with an early-stage compensation model weighted heavily toward ownership and revenue creation rather than a conventional executive salary.
The ability to operate as a principal, not an employee — making decisions with the long-term value of the company in mind and doing whatever work is necessary at this stage to move it forward.

Early-stage go-to-market leadership, experience selling AI or automation products, and experience selling into the legal profession are strongly preferred. Candidates should be able to operate effectively across North American time zones.

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About UJA Federation Of Greater Toronto

At UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, our vision is to lead the most vibrant Jewish community in North America — a community characterized by its diversity, unity, compassion, generosity and commitment to Jewish values. Together with our philanthropic, volunteer and professional leadership, we're changing lives.

As one of North America's leading Jewish non-profits, UJA Federation of Greater Toronto works to preserve and strengthen the quality of Jewish life in Greater Toronto, Canada, Israel and around the world. UJA advances this mission through fundraising, planning, and research focused on our strategic pillars: fighting poverty and improving well-being, growing Jewish education and identity, countering antisemitism and hate, and strengthening connections with Israel and Jewish communities worldwide.

About The Opportunity

At a pivotal time for UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, the Chief Financial Officer serves as a strategic partner to the President & CEO, Chief Operating Officer, Board, and senior leadership team. Building on a stable financial foundation and a capable finance team, the CFO is responsible for advancing finance into a forward-looking enterprise function focused on planning, resource allocation, decision support, organizational performance, and long-term financial sustainability. Initially, the CFO will work closely with the existing team to understand how work is currently performed, strengthen accountability and capability, and create the foundation for a more scalable and strategic finance function. The role exists to ensure that financial insight, forecasting, scenario analysis, performance measurement, and resource allocation effectively support organizational priorities and decision-making. The CFO will develop trusted relationships across professional leadership, Board and committee members, lay leaders, donors, partner agencies, and other key stakeholders, while leading improvements in analytics, systems, data, and processes that strengthen organizational effectiveness and scalability. Success in this role will depend on sound judgment, strong relationships, and the ability to build alignment across a complex stakeholder environment.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Lead the Finance function across UJA entities and operating activities, with accountability for financial stewardship, planning, reporting, controls and team performance.
Own and lead the annual budget process and strengthen multi-year planning, forecasting and scenario analysis, aligning financial plans with strategic priorities.
Lead resource allocation, reserve strategy and long-term sustainability planning, helping leadership assess competing priorities and strengthen UJA's financial resilience.
Oversee investments and organizational assets, working with relevant Board committees and advisors to ensure sound governance, risk management and long-term stewardship.
Lead financial reporting and discussions with the Board and relevant committees, providing clear context, insight and recommendations to support decision-making.
Oversee the annual audit, internal controls, governance and compliance with internal requirements and external obligations, including CRA requirements.
Ensure financial or other risks are appropriately identified, understood and addressed.
Lead, mentor and develop the finance team, establishing clear accountabilities, succession depth and a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.
Champion systems, data and process improvements and strengthen financial acumen across the organization.

Qualifications:

CPA designation.
Senior financial leadership experience, ideally as a CFO or equivalent, within a complex organization with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated success as a strategic partner to a CEO, senior leadership team and Board, with the judgment to influence effectively without relying solely on formal authority.
Proven ability to succeed in a consensus-driven environment and build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.
Board experience is highly valued, particularly with philanthropic or community organizations that combine fundraising with meaningful operating activities.
Track record of developing high-performance finance teams, developing leaders and leading thoughtful organizational change without creating unnecessary disruption.
Strong governance, investment oversight, risk and analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate financial information into clear implications and choices for non-financial stakeholders.
Strategic in orientation while sufficiently hands-on to understand the function, people and processes during a period of transition and evolution.
Passion for UJA’s mission and an appreciation for the complexity of serving a broad and highly engaged community.
This is a full-time position. This posting complies with applicable Ontario employment legislation regarding compensation disclosure requirements.

UJA supports a flexible work schedule and all of our employees engage in hybrid work. Engagement and connection are key to supporting the best employee experience and we want to ensure that this puts balance and well-being at the forefront of our approach to ways of working. In addition to a rich time off policy, UJA's offices are closed on all Jewish holy days (yom tov) and we support early office closures to observe the Jewish Sabbath (Shabbat).

Qualified applicants are invited to submit a cover letter and resume. Only those applicants invited for interview will be contacted. Please be advised that all offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of professional references and background checks including Social Media Account(s) and a Police Records Check/Vulnerable Sector Screening.

Commitment to Inclusion and Accessibility:

UJA Federation supports a diverse candidate and employment experience. We are proud of our dynamic professional team, which reflects the diversity of the Jewish community and general community alike in Greater Toronto. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all communities. We encourage you to follow us to get regular updates on open roles. We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace and believe this is essential to ensure that every member of our team can thrive.

We adhere to barrier-free and accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Should you require Code-protected accommodation through any stage of the recruitment process, please notify us and we will work with you to meet your needs.

We are looking for a Director, Technical Solutions – Enterprise Application Integrations

The Director, Technical Solutions – Enterprise Application Integrations will lead teams responsible for designing and delivering the integration capabilities that connect our applications, data and digital experiences.

This is a leadership role spanning delivery, technology, engineering, and people. The Director will help shape our enterprise integration strategy and engineering practices, enabling teams across Canada Life to build and consume secure, resilient and reusable business capabilities.

What You Will Do

Lead engineering teams responsible for the design, development, delivery and support of enterprise integration solutions, including APIs, microservices, event-driven integrations and other integration patterns.
Build strong relationships with business and technology partners, understanding their priorities and delivering integration solutions that enable their initiatives and business outcomes.
Help shape and execute the technical strategy and roadmap for Enterprise Application Integration, aligned with enterprise architecture and business priorities.
Drive the modernisation of integration solutions, increasing the use of API-led, event-driven and cloud-native approaches while reducing legacy complexity and technical debt.
Establish and champion engineering standards, reusable patterns and reference architectures that improve consistency, security, resilience and speed of delivery.
Provide technical leadership on complex initiatives, guiding architecture and engineering decisions across integration, APIs, microservices and distributed systems.
Strengthen engineering excellence and operational resilience through DevSecOps, automation, testing, observability and strong production practices.
Partner across Architecture, Integration Platforms, Cloud, Cyber Security, Data and application teams to deliver secure, scalable and reliable solutions.
Build and develop high-performing engineering teams, growing technical capability, developing leaders and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

What You Will Bring

Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Proven technology and engineering leadership experience, including leading and developing high-performing teams.
Strong delivery leadership, with the ability to translate business priorities into technology outcomes and drive complex initiatives through to delivery.
Strong knowledge of enterprise integration and distributed systems, including APIs, microservices, event-driven architecture and modern integration patterns.

Experience coaching and developing technical leaders and practitioners, creating an environment of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to make complex technology topics understandable to both technical and non-technical audiences.
A bias for action, curiosity and critical thinking, with the ability to adapt quickly as business and technology priorities evolve.
A growth mindset and willingness to challenge existing approaches, experiment and continuously improve how teams work and deliver.
Experience working in the financial services, insurance or wealth management industry.
Hands-on experience earlier in your career in software development, solution architecture, systems analysis or another technical engineering discipline.
Experience with cloud technologies and modern cloud architectures.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and global delivery models.
Experience with product-oriented technology delivery or product management practices.
Experience driving DevSecOps, automation, observability, reliability and operational excellence within engineering organisations.
Experience using engineering, delivery and operational metrics to understand performance, identify opportunities and drive continuous improvement.
Knowledge of insurance and wealth business domains and the technology ecosystems that support them.

jobs.title: Director of Sales, Enterprise
jobs.description:
Dot Compliance is a leading provider of cloud-based Quality and Compliance Management solutions for the Life Sciences industry. Built on Salesforce, our innovative SaaS platform helps pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies streamline and transform their quality and compliance processes.
We are a growing, innovative software company on a mission to change how regulated Life Sciences organizations manage quality and compliance worldwide.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Sales, Enterprise

to lead and grow our enterprise sales business across North America.
In this role, you will be responsible for driving new business revenue within the Enterprise segment across North America, developing and executing strategic sales plans, and leading a team of Account Executives to consistently achieve ambitious revenue targets.
You are a hands-on sales leader who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth SaaS environment. You bring deep experience navigating complex enterprise sales cycles, building relationships with senior decision-makers, and successfully closing high-value deals involving multiple stakeholders.
You will work closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to strengthen our enterprise sales capabilities, expand our presence within large Life Sciences organizations, and build a predictable, scalable enterprise revenue engine across North America.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Revenue Growth:

Own and execute the North American enterprise sales plan to achieve new business ARR targets, expand market share, and drive sustainable revenue growth across strategic enterprise accounts.
Enterprise Sales Strategy:

Develop and implement structured sales approaches tailored to complex enterprise buying cycles, including account planning, opportunity qualification, stakeholder mapping, and deal execution.
Team Leadership & Coaching:

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Account Executives. Provide hands-on coaching, performance management, and support throughout the sales process to consistently achieve revenue targets.
Strategic Deal Management:

Actively participate in complex, high-value sales opportunities, supporting the team with deal strategy, executive engagement, negotiations, procurement processes, and closing.
Executive Relationship Building:

Establish and strengthen relationships with senior executives and key stakeholders within large pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device organizations across the US and Canada.
Pipeline & Sales Performance:

Build and maintain a healthy enterprise sales pipeline, monitor key performance metrics, and identify opportunities to improve win rates, deal progression, and overall sales effectiveness.
Market Development:

Identify and pursue new enterprise opportunities across North America, developing targeted account strategies and strengthening Dot Compliance's positioning within the Life Sciences industry.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:

Partner closely with Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Revenue Operations to align enterprise go-to-market initiatives, support complex customer requirements, and deliver effective sales execution.
Forecasting & Reporting:

Drive accurate revenue forecasting, strategic pipeline reviews, and sales reporting, providing senior leadership with clear visibility into opportunities, risks, and expected revenue performance.

Requirements:

What We're Looking For

8+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales focused on Enterprise accounts
3+ years in management or leadership roles, leading, managing, and coaching Account Executives, including supporting strategic deal execution and performance development.
Proven track record of achieving and exceeding enterprise sales targets within the North American and Global markets, with demonstrated success closing complex, high-value SaaS deals.
Experience selling SaaS solutions into Life Sciences, Quality Management, Compliance, or other highly regulated industries. 
Possessing a strong understanding of how international pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies operate, including their global regulatory and compliance pain points (e.g., FDA, EMA, GxP). 
Strong understanding of complex enterprise sales cycles, including multi-stakeholder decision-making, executive-level selling, procurement, and contract negotiations.
Well-developed business acumen and the ability to engage effectively with C-level executives and senior decision-makers, translating technical capabilities into measurable business value.
Hands-on leadership style, with the ability to guide sales teams through qualification, discovery, value-based selling, negotiation, and closing.
Strong analytical skills and experience with revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and sales performance metrics.
Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-growing environment, balancing strategic thinking with hands-on sales execution.
Availability to work primarily Eastern Time (ET) hours is required to effectively collaborate with internal teams.

Great Attributes

Experience selling Quality Management Systems (QMS), or other compliance software.
Experience scaling enterprise sales teams and processes within early-to-mid-stage SaaS companies.
Familiarity with Salesforce-native SaaS products and go-to-market environments.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics
new_jobs.description:
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.

Job Purpose

This role exists to strengthen how the North America Foods business plans, decides, and delivers across demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and business waste. As Associate Director, S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics, you will lead the planning excellence and analytics agenda that connects business ambition with practical, reliable operating plans. You will help build a more resilient, data-driven, and collaborative supply chain that enables trusted Foods brands to serve customers and consumers with confidence. This is inclusive of planning technology, analytics, and process.

You will be part of a team that believes planning is more than a process. It is a critical way of bringing people together, making better decisions, and creating the conditions for sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead the development and continuous improvement of integrated planning and sales and operations planning practices across North America Foods (Retail and Foods Solutions; US and Canada). You will partner closely with Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Material Planning, Manufacturing, Finance, Customer Development, Marketing, and senior Supply Chain leaders to ensure the business has clear plans, strong governance, reporting/tools, and actionable insights to support growth, service, efficiency, and transformation.

Lead a team of WL1s/2s to drive the sales and operations planning excellence agenda. Ensure robust process and technology are in place to ensure demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and financial assumptions are connected through clear business rhythms and decision-making forums.
Partner with integrated planning teams to identify risks, opportunities, and gaps within planning technology/process and drive improvement plans. Identify / build business cases or drive cross functional process improvement.
Strengthen integrated planning capability by improving processes, tools, routines, governance, and ways of working across the North America Foods planning community.
Lead planning performance management, including the maintenance and creation and use of clear measures, scorecards, dashboards, reports, and insights that help teams make faster and better decisions. This can include modifying existing dashboards due to new business insights
Drive continuous improvement, simplification, and standardization across planning processes to improve reliability, reduce complexity, and support scalable ways of working.
Act as the primary point of contact for Planning TSAs.
Support the transition to the future Foods organization by helping design, build, and embed planning capabilities that enable business continuity from day one and maturity over time.
Build trusted relationships across functions and levels, creating a collaborative planning culture where teams are aligned, accountable, and focused on shared outcomes.

What The First Year Looks Like

During the first year, you will play a visible role in building planning excellence for the future North America Foods organization. You will learn the current planning landscape, connect with key partners across the business, and help establish the routines, measures, and decision-making forums needed to support business continuity and performance.

In your first few months, you will focus on understanding the end-to-end planning processes, key business priorities, current pain points, and transition requirements. You will build relationships with the planning community, data/tech teams, and cross-functional partners, assess existing tools and processes, and identify where stronger governance or simplification is needed.

As the year progresses, you will lead improvements to planning routines, performance reporting, and sales and operations planning governance. You will help teams align on clear roles, timelines, inputs, decisions, and escalation paths, while supporting capability-building across the planning organization.

By the end of the first year, you will have helped create a stronger integrated planning foundation for North America Foods, with clearer decision-making, improved planning visibility, stronger cross-functional alignment, and practical tools that support service, inventory, cost, waste reduction, and growth.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Engineering, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Strong understanding of sales and operations planning, forecasting, inventory management, capacity planning, supply planning, service management, and business waste reduction.
Experience leading cross-functional planning decisions and balancing service, inventory, cost, responsiveness, and growth priorities.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear business recommendations.
Experience influencing senior stakeholders and leading change in a complex, fast-moving environment.
Demonstrated ability to build capability, improve processes, and create practical ways of working that teams can adopt and sustain.
Strong understanding of planning tools and technology including back end master data.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in consumer goods, food and beverage, manufacturing, retail, or another complex supply chain environment.
Experience leading sales and operations planning improvements, integrated planning transformation, or planning excellence programs across multiple teams or markets.
Experience with advanced planning systems, enterprise resource planning systems, business intelligence tools, or planning analytics platforms.
Experience supporting organization transition, business separation, integration, or large-scale transformation activities.
Advanced degree or professional certification in supply chain, operations, planning, project management, or continuous improvement.
